SiteTopo 3D – quick guide

  1. Site – search an address, PID, title (e.g. 133100/1), lat, lon or E N (MGA2020 zone 55). The LIST parcel is loaded as the subject boundary. Use “Draw boundary” for lots not yet in the cadastre.
  2. Offline data – “Link data folder…” (step 1) points the tool at the folder filled by Download Tasmanian data.bat: the MRT statewide 2 m DEM and the LIST parcels, address points, contours and landslide planning map. Chrome / Edge remember the folder; each session asks once to allow access. The 2 m DEM is read straight from the folder (only the site’s window); the LIST layers are used when the LIST website cannot be reached, or always if you choose “First”. Without the folder the 2 m DEM is streamed from the internet. Saved projects keep the site’s photo, elevation grid, boundaries, landslip map and coastal data, so they reopen without internet.
  3. Field data – drop CSV/TXT, Moasure CSV/DXF, GPX/KML or GeoJSON, or paste from Excel. Columns are detected automatically; check them on the data card. Local X/Y data (e.g. Moasure) need placing: pick the origin on the map and set the rotation, or use “Place by two known points”.
  4. Transects – chainage/RL tables. Lines named A–D are placed by default through the middle of the lot with chainage 0 where the line enters the boundary: A W→E, B N→S, C NW→SE, D NE→SW. Adjust the start, bearing or chainage at start if your line differs, or click “Pick start & direction on map”. One spreadsheet holding several lines (a Line/Transect column with A, B, C…) is split automatically.
  5. Levels – per dataset choose: as recorded (AHD), fit to the background surface (least-squares offset, optionally using only points outside the boundary), tie to a benchmark (point = known RL) or a manual offset.
  6. Surface – the background DEM (MRT 2 m DEM, GA 5 m LiDAR, LIST contours, AWS SRTM tiles or your own DEM) is corrected by your data: inside the data area the surface honours your levels exactly; the correction fades to zero over the blend distance. GPS-grade sets can be smoothed instead.
  7. Landslip & sections – step 6 loads the LIST Landslide Planning Map (hazard bands + MRT components), reports what intersects the lot and exports a landslip sheet. Add test holes (Hole, E, N, From, To, Unit) to build layered sections along the transects or your own lines; export DXF (Slide2 / SLOPE/W), CSV and a section sheet.
  8. Report figures – the header button exports the Foundation Assessment template figure set in one go: Fig1a site plan (aerial, holes, DCPs, services), Fig1b location within the suburb (1:5000), Fig1f landslide hazard bands, Fig1g contours with the lot’s elevation range, one figure per test hole with its log beside the nearby DCP on the same depth axis (DCP #n goes with THn; rows under 100 kPa by the template’s n × 30 shaded, dashed 100 kPa line), the 3D view and section sheets, plus captions.txt (template captions filled in, DCP offsets for the table captions, landslip summary, nearest services). Uses the current 2D plan settings (paper, scale, dpi). Chrome / Edge: pick the job folder; otherwise a ZIP downloads.
  9. Boundary style – step 1: colour, shading and a white or dark edge so the lot stands out on any background; used on the map, in 3D and on every sheet (the landslip sheet keeps an outline only).
  10. Simulations – step 7 runs screening models on the merged surface: infinite-slope factor of safety (mean, lower bound and Monte Carlo probability of FoS < 1, as SAGA SAFETYFACTOR), SHALSTAB critical rainfall (as GRASS r.shalstab), GPP random-walk run-out (as SAGA sim_geomorphology) and an indicative single-phase Voellmy mass flow (like r.avaflow), animated in 3D and exportable as a video (MP4 in Chrome / Edge). Draw release areas, or use cells with FoS < 1 or the LIST source areas. “Export run package” writes the DEM, release and soil-depth grids with ready-to-run run_saga.bat / run_grass.bat scripts and r.avaflow inputs; drop their GeoTIFF / ASC results back on step 7 to show them in 3D and on the sheet.
  11. Survey plans – step 1 › “Load plan (PDF / image)…”: choose the sheet, drag a box round the drawing, then click two boundary corners on the plan and the same two on the map. The plan snaps to every LIST parcel corner it matches and shows over the aerial on the map, in 3D and on the 2D plan (colour and opacity on its card). “Use as boundary” makes a lot from the plan the site boundary – for subdivisions not yet in the LIST.
  12. Coastal hazards & tides – step 6 reads the coastal copy in the data folder (Data\COAST, filled by Download Tasmanian data.bat; the coastal part uses the GDAL tools that come with QGIS): the LIST coastal inundation and erosion hazard bands, erosion component, projected storm tide (1% AEP 2010 / 2050 / 2100), sea level rise and shoreline types; DEA Coastlines (annual shorelines since 1988, rates of change, hotspots); DEA Intertidal (elevation, HAT / LAT) and the AIMS tide statistics. Tick what to show on the map, in 3D and on the 2D plan. The coastal summary says which bands reach the lot (or how far away the nearest is), the storm tide and band levels, the nearest shoreline type, how far the DEA shoreline has moved, the tide levels and the lowest ground against them – “Copy” puts it on the clipboard. Ticked levels show on sections and as see-through water in 3D. “Export coastal sheet” and the report figures (Coastal_1 … Coastal_7) frame the lot with the nearest mapping, over a wider aerial when online. Heights: LIST m AHD; DEA / AIMS relative to modelled mean sea level (set the local MSL above AHD to convert). Planning-scale, indicative mapping.
  13. Services – step 1 › Services loads TasWater water, sewer and stormwater (and, if ticked, TasNetworks power and gas) for the site automatically – from the LIST, or from the data folder when offline. They show on the map, in 3D, on the 2D plan and on sections (sewer / stormwater inverts where TasWater records them). “Nearest services to the boundary” gives distance, side, size and material (and sewer invert depth) – “Copy” puts it on the clipboard for the report. Positions are indicative; confirm with Dial Before You Dig.
  14. GIS export – the header button writes a folder with a QGIS project (double-click to open): test holes, DCPs, layer logs, DCP readings, site points, boundary, the LIST parcels and any survey plans, styled and labelled, in GDA2020 / MGA. Each layer is also a GeoJSON with its own style file.
  15. Measure – “📏 Measure” (tab bar) works on the map and in the 3D view. Distance: click two or more points – length per leg and in total, bearing (grid and true), RL change, grade, the length along the ground and a profile. Area: click the corners (click the first one again, double-click or Enter to finish) – area in m² / ha, perimeter, the ground-surface area following the slope, mean slope and RL range. Lot outline: click inside a LIST parcel or a survey-plan lot to take its outline. Clicks snap to parcel and plan-lot corners, test holes and earlier points (hold Alt to place freely). Values are ground distances (MGA2020 grid ÷ scale factor). “Keep” saves a measurement with the project; kept ones show on the map, in 3D and on the 2D plan (step 5 › Measurements), and can be copied as text, turned into a section line or made the site boundary.
  16. What’s here – click the map, or the ground in the 3D view, to list everything shown at that point: coastal hazard bands, DEA shorelines with their years and how far each is from the click, shoreline change rates, services, the landslide planning map, the parcel (address, PID, title), test holes and DCPs close by (click one for its log), and the ground (RL, slope and the way it falls, MGA2020 and GDA2020 coordinates). In 3D a pin marks the spot and the card sits at the top left beside the hole card.
  17. Site library – the header button “Library” opens the file of every logged site (“SiteTopo site library - all sites.json” in the X-Safe Folder): one record per site with its test-hole logs, DCP readings, lab results and positions, from the Soil Database, the report figures and the phone records. It is kept on this computer after the first “Open file…” (or drop the file on the map). Search by ID, address, suburb, firm or class; filter own reports, other firms or phone records. Sites show on the map (green own, amber other firms, blue phone records); click one for its details. Open shows a site with the logged sites within 400 m (a subdivision opens as one; a site reporting the same holes as another is left out); + adds a nearby site to the one in view. The eye switches a site on or off – on the map here and, once loaded, in 3D, the 2D plan, sections and report figures (the same switch as in step 6). Positions are GDA2020; most are digitised from report figures and carry their precision (±2–10 m) in each hole's notes. On a phone: “Site library” on the Field screen (or “Open a site file…” with the library file) opens the same list; the map and hole cards fill the screen, and the file stays on the phone.
  18. Show / hide holes – step 6 lists the sites with their holes and DCPs. The eye on a site, a hole or the “Test holes” / “DCPs” ticks hides them from the map, 3D, 2D plan, sections and report figures without removing them from the project; ◎ shows only that site; ✕ removes a site. Sites fold up (▸) so long lists stay short.
  19. Paper log sheets – print the field log sheet v2 (the one with black squares in the corners). On the phone, a site's “Paper sheets” card photographs a filled-in sheet: it is straightened, the page is recognised, ticked boxes and circled Y / N are read and fill empty fields (tap to correct; orange = check it), rows with writing become layers of the hole you choose, and the sheet is kept as a photo of that hole – each layer shows its strip of the sheet while you type it in, and each DCP its column. For the handwriting, “Package for Claude” makes a ZIP to give to Claude (Cowork); the transcription file Claude returns can be opened on the phone or dropped here, and every change is listed before anything is saved.
  20. Rename – click the project name in the header (or ✎ in step 1) to rename the project: titles, report figures and file names follow. ✎ on a site in step 6 corrects a field site's address (e.g. a lot number typed wrongly on the phone); the correction is kept with the project and on this computer whenever that site is imported again.
  21. Soft ground (v2.5) – step 4 › “Colour DCPs by”: Soft readings in the window (the share of 100 mm readings at 3 blows or fewer – about 90 kPa or less on the 30 × blows rule), Mean blows in the window or Depth reached. The window is 0.6–1.4 m unless you change it; a DCP needs 4 readings in it to be rated (grey = too shallow). The colours show on the map (with a legend), in 3D (discs outside the window grey), on the 2D plan and on the hole card; sections colour the bars ≤ 3 / 4–5 / 6+ blows and shade the window. Display only – no bearing values are implied. Step 4 › Overlay › Terrain lows – old channels shades ground lower (blue) or higher (orange) than the ground within about 30 m (surface minus its 30 m Gaussian average); Flow paths & ponding shows where runoff gathers (wider = more ground draining through) and the hollows that would pond. Both show in 3D, on the map, and on the plan with “Use 3D overlay”; hover in 3D or click (What’s here) for the values at a point.
  22. Lab results (v2.5) – Field › open the site › “Lab results from the calc workbook…”: choose the job’s Template_3 workbook (.xlsm). LL, PL, PI, LS and the lab USCS class are read for every sample on the TH Report tab (LS from RAW DATA), matched to the site’s samples by hole and depth, and added after you tick them; the class also goes on the layers each sample spans. Save the workbook in Excel after entering lab data – the values Excel saved are the ones read. A copy of the site is kept under Earlier versions first.
  23. Phone and laptop (v2.5) – a site corrected on the laptop and then updated on the phone is merged, not replaced: changes made on one side only come in by themselves; a value changed on both is listed so you can choose (the laptop’s is ticked). A copy is kept under Earlier versions before every merge.
  24. Landslide risk (v2.6) – step 8 and the Risk tab: the AGS (2007c) risk assessment. Add one row per mechanism × receptor × state (existing, construction, operation, with treatment). A property row takes a likelihood (A almost certain 10⁻¹ … F barely credible 10⁻⁶) and a consequence (1 catastrophic 200 % … 5 insignificant 0.5 % of property value) and reads the level from the matrix; a life row takes P(H) (the descriptor’s value unless you type one), P(S:H), P(T:S) and V(D:T) and gives R(LOL). Risk to life is summed per person in each state and compared with 10⁻⁵ per annum. Rows can be linked to holes, DCPs, sections and drawn features; ⧉ copies a row to the states not yet rated. The sensitivity check scales one input (× 0.5 to × 10) and says whether any state’s conclusion changes. Matrix and scales are editable – check them against your SOP. “Copy tables for Word” pastes formatted tables; “Export CSV” gives every input and result. The tables are saved in the project file only.
  25. Outputs – 3D PNG at up to 4800 px, and a scaled 2D plan (A4/A3, 300 dpi) with contours over the aerial photo. PNGs carry their DPI so they insert at the right size in Word.

Background contours are indicative and only as good as the source DEM. Check field datum ties before relying on absolute levels.

Paste table

Paste rows from Excel or a text file (with or without headers). Columns are detected automatically.
